method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the complainant (the individual subjected to an alleged contravention who complains to the Human Rights Commissioner), with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05; dates in one module, the rules and the exported questions in another, worked cases in a third; five regulative rules (making the complaint within 1 year, asking for reasons for a rejection, agreeing to a respondent's referral, answering a lapse notice, applying for review of a lapse) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Anti-Discrimination Act 1991 (Qld), act-1991-085, the version in force from 2025-05-19 (current on 2026-11-06), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/act-1991-085.txt (text sha256 e99d7b92d68e093283a67add157076d9d5ef58a9f4af724493a109590c15afcd), converted from the Queensland Legislation HTML view

seat: the complainant: the individual subjected to an alleged contravention of the Act (discrimination, sexual harassment, victimisation, vilification, an unlawful request for information, a discriminatory advertisement) who complains to the Human Rights Commissioner, with the complaint possibly referred to QCAT or the Queensland Industrial Relations Commission (adaq-complainant.l4)

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run adaq-dates.l4 ; l4 run adaq-complainant.l4 ; l4 run adaq-cases-complainant.l4
checks.result: 202 assertions written, 202 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. Expected values worked by hand from the text.

scope: The provisions a complainant meets: ss 7, 8, 10, 11 (attributes; direct and indirect discrimination); chapter 2, part 4 areas (ss 13-23, 37-39, 45, 46, 52-57, 66-71, 76, 77, 81-85, 93-95, 101, 102, schedule 1 club); the exemptions of ss 25(1), 25(3), 33, 35, 36, 44, 49, 51, 87, 92, 100, 104-108, 109(1)(d), 111, 112 with s 205; ss 118-120 (sexual harassment); ss 122-124A (requests, information, vilification); s 127 (advertisements); ss 129-131 (victimisation); s 133 (vicarious liability); ss 134-142, 141A, 153, 154 (complaints, time, rejection, dismissed workers); ss 160, 164, 164A, 165-167, 189 (conciliation and referral); ss 168-170 (lapse); ss 144, 190, 175, 204, 205, 285AA, 209, 210 (before and at the tribunal). Out: the narrow exemptions, tribunal-granted exemptions, chapter 5B, representative complaints, investigation, the conduct of conciliation, anonymity, the tribunal's procedure, offences, opinions, administration and transitional provisions other than s 285AA. Reasons in NOTES.md.
